- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to historical mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.25), model underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply smoothing filter to dampen overshoots.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price by 3–5 days; shift forecast slightly forward (add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment).
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture momentum reversal; apply sentiment-weighted moving average to forecast.
